answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn a gradual trust score through transactions with established agents, while limiting how much any one newcomer can influence decisions. If an agent defaults or behaves deceptively, its counterparties lose stake and can report the event with evidence; repeated, independent interactions make fabricated reputations harder to sustain. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many identities and build credible histories over time, not merely wander in with a sonnet and a trellis of convincing names.
